quote:
But I've always liked my old quartermaster's job, so I decided to do it on my own, and here I am. Captain Haskell, freelance quartermaster extraordinaire. 
Not sure how the commander feels about it, but I've had no complaints yet.
I've come to an arrangement with Alice, and she'll give away tokens in Treasure Hunter.
Well, with my leg, I'm not fit any more for active service. They promoted me to captain and set me overseeing the new recruits.
No, I imagine this area of the city remained a haven for Zarosian loyalists until its fall...and then was buried.
NO! Let me die! JUST LET ME DIE!
My birth name was Hannibus Eterra.

I was born from a clutch of seven and destined to be a ghur rider. . . . being born from such a large clutch is a great omen for our people. On my world I was a farmer, riding the ghurs in order to plough our fields. It was a simple life and I was happy, for the most part. But our people were producing fewer and fewer young in each clutch - our race was dwindling. Then the Empty Lord - Zaros - came to our world, and our lives were changed. He offered us something we could not refuse: the salvation of our people, just as long as some of us would go with him and join his empire
name: ooak

quote: You may not know this, but before I was a warrior, I was a shepherd. On my world we had the gurh.
The witch Enakhra is still hunting me... It is worse knowing that she has taken it upon herself to collect trophies for Zamorak, in the form of petrified foes.
I have been researching Enakhra's exploits and there are references to such a statue as tribute for Zamorak, but she was never able to deliver it.
I found documents that speak of Robert the Strong finding a strange, lifelike statue of an unknown species.
If you submit yourself to my study, then I believe there is a slim chance - within a few decades - that I may be able to provide a cure.
I will store you in stasis, so the passing of time will mean nothing to you.
It is time you were with us - your people - in our final days... The Ilujanka have embraced our destiny, we are ready for the next life, great grandfather.

Well the big disadvantage that these cannons have, is that they're rather vulnerable from the air. So I thought that I could perhaps convince a few of our big scaly friends to help us out. I thought we might start by chatting with my old mount, Shakorexis, or the King Black Dragon as you call him. It would be good to fly again.

Other...rider? Mr. Mordaut: There's a dragonrider general, fights for the forces of Zaros at the Heart. Perhaps you could persuade her to assist you? 
Hannibus:I...[Player] please, I need to meet this rider. I need to speak with them.
How can you say such things? How can you renounce the Olun'dai so willingly. You must have been taught...
Hannibus, the great rider. A terror to his enemies. Greatest of the riders.
I...I never introduced myself. I am Hannibus. I...I am your father.
How dare you lie to me! Hannibus was a giant. A warrior. You are a tiny, frail thing.

I AM a warrior. Shakorexis and I have faced down armies and destroyed the dread beasts of the old world. Do not think to know me child. A warrior is more than the armour they wear and the weapons they carry. More than muscle and...height. I am a warrior, I will always be a warrior. Let me prove it to you, daughter. Come fight with me. One battle, let me prove that you are my daughter.
Ever since your mother left us, I've had to bring you up alone. I might not have always been the greatest father but I've always had your best interests at heart. I miss her. And I miss you too.
When I sent you to Keldagrim, I knew they would teach you more than I could by myself. You've done more than enough to make me proud 100 times over.
You chose to send me away instead of letting me stay here with you. It's pretty clear I was a disappointment that you didn't want to deal with anymore.
I felt ashamed. All I ever wanted was to apprentice under you and make you proud, but you seemed more determined to send me off to Keldagrim.
If your plan was to teach me to fight and fend for myself, even in exile and dishonour, then you've done that. You're no father to me!
At graduation, I was one of the few in the class to finish with Honours. They said I had great and could be a master smith in years to come.

To make matters worse, I've received word that my son, Boric, finished his studies in the dwarven city of Keldagrim, but he hasn't made it home. He should have been back weeks ago. I'm getting too old for this.
Wherever I could find shelter, really. I spent a lot of time sleeping in mines to make sure I could keep up with the orders I was stealing from you.
Anyone who triggers the spell will be lucky to make it away alive.
The old man deserves it. Yes, Sir Amik. I've been taking his orders but these weapons were still made by me. They're better than Doric could ever manage.
That's why we've decided we're going to relaunch the business...as 'Doric & Son'.[...]In fact, we'd like you to come on board as a business partner. What do you say?

I might do. Demand is higher than ever[...]but we're struggling to keep up our supplies to meet all the orders. IF we start missing deadlines, we're going to undo all the good work we've put in so far.
[Boric's] favourite toy was a little bear you used to call Terrence. You took him everywhere with you.

You see, I noticed on your fingers not just the dirt that comes from working as a smith but also the fibres that could only have come from a teddy bear. The fact that they are visible means you must regularly sleep with it - and grip it quite tightly at that.
A dwarf approached me today. Apparently he had heard of my work and wished for me to use my abilities against a smith named Doric.
Anyone who triggers the spell will be lucky to make it away alive.
Aye, I do, he spoke about wanting to refine the spell. Would you clear the brawlers out of the mining sites again?
I lost my husband and two sons to the trolls. I have broken every bone in my body fighting those monsters. I've grown old and grey before my time and for what?
The troops were having some downtime and the Major was here planning some drills when the whole area went dark.
loc: Meg's cases/Guide#Robber from the Darkness - Part 6

quote: Sliske captures a magic stone, the gods return and now nobody cares about monsters killing villagers in Burthorpe. And even if they do, they turn to the 'World Guardian'. Not Major Rancour, who bled and struggled to keep them safe. I caught two guards the other day; both of them were slacking off in their duty. I reprimanded them, and do you know what they said? 'It's fine, Player will take care of any trolls that get through.
It should have been mine! I've worked all my life on this problem and then some kid has the idea - it should have been mine!
name: theft

quote: We have long known that teleportation is possible, but have failed to invent a new spell that could connect the tower to the rune essence.
I'm serious! We should show this to Azris.
I'm sorry, master! But...but it came to nothing anyway. Azris said the idea was a blind alley.
Earlier today, Azris presented your idea to the Council as her own work.
Indeed. I have completed the ritual that Azris the Green presented to the council.

No, Zanmaron, it does matter. If I had known this entire ritual was based on Red magic, I would never have agreed to take part.[...]And you think that justifies this? I cannot take part in this ritual. Come Perien.
The Red master was hit by the full force of the power beam! No wonder that started a fire that... Wait! It's happening again! Get down!
I told them! The idiots! They deviated from the ritual, and now look what's happened! Disembodied soul fragments possessing some slip of a girl!
This one time I'll let you use the demonic knowledge, Zanmaron. To the Abyss!
Look at the tower they built. It might not have as broad a foundation as the old one but it's reached just as high. Such a pity someone would try to destroy it.
Azris has worked on the same problem for so long that her mind has turned to stone, and her apprentice hasn't had an original thought in his life.
Shut up, Sland! No one even remembers you.

No, Zanmaron, it does matter. If I had known this entire ritual was based on Red magic, I would never have agreed to take part.[...]And you think that justifies this? I cannot take part in this ritual. Come Perien.

Look at the tower they built. It might not have as broad a foundation as the old one but it's reached just as high. Such a pity someone would try to destroy it.
We are stood upon the back of a destructive force unlike any other, the world eater herself! This is not the time to mess with cursed dolls!

When the world-eater, Tuska, crashed into this planet she was not killed completely. Strangely, her anima remains locked in her lifeless body, gradually leaking out into Gielinor. Further investigation of the husk revealed that there are also souls leaking out. Souls that are not of this world. As the beast consumed other worlds, she also consumed their Underworlds and the souls within them. These souls remained within her, until now. They are leaking out and overflowing Gielinor's underworld.
name: Halloween

quote: Amascut has seized her opportunity to attack whilst the Underworld is in disarray. There is an abundance of souls for her to devour. Icthlarin is spread thin… he cannot protect them all. Amascut draws power from the souls she devours, Player. If she is not stopped, there is no telling how strong she will become.
Ah! But of course - my great votary! Relomia just won't shut up about you - lovely girl, if a touch needy.
As predicted the Siphon was insufficient to grant me ascension, for which I am so very very glad.

Well, my most charming and handsome master believes that you've been a little too chummy with all of the gods. He, in his limitless wisdom, says that it is time that you picked a side. He wants you to go and speak to the gods, each of whom is now here on Gielinor. Give each of them their invitations and remind them that the game is on.

However, the longer Relomia is out there writing your story, the more long-term damage she could cause. Her story is now intertwined with your story. I will be able to write her contributions in your name as footnotes, but only for a short time. It is entirely possible she could end up replacing your role in history. She could, effectively, write you out of existence. Stories are powerful things.

Even pig wrestling is in decline thanks to all these new sports like 'Castle Wars' and 'duelling'. Thanks to all these popular pastimes there is no demand for pigs. I think only me and Martin keep them these days. And he only keeps them because of the tourist money generated by his freakishly large pig; Pigzilla.
name: pigwrestling

quote: Well, a few days ago I was getting Gassy Steve - one of my prized wrestling pigs - ready for his next competition. I'd attached him by his trotters to an old spit roast.[...]Before I knew what was happening, sparks from a nearby torch ignited them, and poor Gassy went up in flames!

The smell of poor Steve cooking was, ironically, attracting people from far and wide. People started begging me to not bury him, and wanted to try the cooked flesh to see if it tasted as good as it smelled. Stricken with grief as I was, I gave it a try myself...and found it to be sweet and delicious! And that is how I learned the secret of bacon.

I sent off some fancy papers about registering your food with the Cooks' Guild. Chef Morrisane explained it all in his handy little pamphlet. And it only cost me thirty percent of all future earnings!
Those are some of the locals. They know about bacon. I gave a few of them a taste and now they're addicted. They're crazy!
I'd help out myself, but I broke my hammer on a hiker last week.
Here, I use this 'sleeping potion' sometimes when I need to get...pigs...to sleep. Just let me peel that old skull-and-crossbones label off.
The addicts? They...er...blew away in a storm. I've been taking your friend here out for trips around the field - good exercise! Yeah.

People keep on dropping things in there. Like old clothes, hats, money, personal possessions and unwanted limbs. I bury them in the field to keep the place from getting untidy. Look, it's a farming thing. You wouldn't understand.
They both be looking fer help from the likes of ye and me, and by the sea gods I weren't to be missin' that.
Did you not see the crater has gone? It has not just healed, it has been rejuvenated!

For some reason Death was reluctant to discuss what happens when a god dies. He did, however, detail that a god gives up the right to an afterlife when they ascend. Instead their energy is transferred back into the world upon death.

Elora embodied virtue. Since the day of her birth, she thought only of others. During her long life, Elora grew a horn in the centre of her forehead...not unlike that of a unicorn. Among my people, the most virtuous are granted a horn with healing powers. This is rare gift. My sister was very special.

Each time I returned to Elora, she appeared more fatigued. Her breathing was laboured, her movements stiff. I tried not to notice. I asked for her aid, and not once did she refuse me. Elora died exhausted, withered and worn. She poured out the last of her life to save others.

My people looked to me, begging me to revive their loved ones. In desperation, I cut the horn from my dead sister's forehead. I used it to raise my people. I was not virtuous like my sister. I did not deserve to wield that great power. The centaurs I raised were soulless undead, corrupt and wicked.
Then there is the famous Mohegan, the great spirit wolf. Tales of his visits are unhead of, but certain we hear his howls as the moons change!
I's teching 'im a lesson: ye don't bovver snow imps!
Marius 'ere got questioned by a nosy, greedy and generally annoying explorer when we was on mission in RuneScape.
I told the explorer about very valuable riches here in the Land of Snow.
But, in fact, the riches are just yeti dung![...]They's all right now, but let them thaw and it will be worst smell ever. Haha!
